RFC8955-3-1.note: Both halves now tagged both ways. Community half: TestRFC8955CommunityPolicyAcceptsAPermittedFlowSpecRoute (ipv4/flow and ipv4/flow-vpn with 65001:100 accepted) and TestRFC8955CommunityPolicyRejectsADeniedFlowSpecRoute (denied community first-match and implicit deny reject a FlowSpec route); revert records on evaluateCommunities. Prefix half: filter_prefix flowspec_test.go pair (accept, reject, missing, mixed), no record. Both at the plugin entry point: no .ci drives a FlowSpec UPDATE through a configured community filter in the running daemon. Rejudged 2026-10-17 (independent reader) after the owner-approved 6019dd0675 change to TestPrefixPolicyFiltersFlowSpecDestination: the filter input prefix changed from nlri to mp, the section keyword the filter text now uses for MP_REACH families. The cases are unchanged: ipv4/flow and ipv4/flow-vpn destinations inside 10.0.0.0/8 ge 16 le 24 must be accepted, and /25, out-of-range, invalid and mixed destinations rejected, with no unicast rewrite. A parser that stopped reading the mp form would fail the accept cases, and a policy that stopped applying would fail the reject cases. Package re-run green 2026-10-17. RFC 8955 Section 3: "Standard BGP policy mechanisms, such as UPDATE filtering by NLRI prefix as well as community matching, must apply to the Flow specification defined NLRI-type." The community units are unchanged. Verdict stands.

RFC8955-4-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 by an independent auditor (authored none of 7b0bf3a723, f70588873f or the row edit), over the requirement now naming two producers. RFC 8955 Section 4: "When advertising Flow Specifications, the Length of the Next-Hop Network Address MUST be set to 0." Row {partial}: tested "MUST be set to 0" (every FlowSpec advertisement with no redirect-to-IP-next-hop 0x0800 community); gap "Length of the Next-Hop Network Address" (a 0x0800 route leaves with the redirect address, owner-approved deviation 2026-10-20/21, draft-simpson-idr-flowspec-redirect-02 Section 3, disclosed in Support remaining, never counted conformant). Producers: internal/component/bgp/message/update_build_plugin.go::MPReachCarriesNextHop on the origination rails, and internal/component/bgp/reactor/peer_forward_facts.go::precomputeRedirectNextHop with forward_next_hop.go::applyRedirectNextHop on the forward rails. The tested scope still holds on the forward rails by construction: under redirectKeep the received hop survives only when redirectActionLeaves finds a 0x0800 in the outgoing extended communities, every other action calls setMPNextHop(nil), and mpReachNextHopHandler keeps a 4- or 16-octet Set only for a FlowSpec family and writes every other width as the empty field. The tests assert exact bytes: assertFlowForwardWire compares the whole MP_REACH value to AFI/SAFI/len 0/reserved/NLRI across unchanged, self, explicit4 and explicit6 with empty, peer-address and IPv6 received hops (TestFlowSpecForwardingOmitsNextHop), so the redirectKeep branch leaking a non-redirect hop would redden the unchanged cases; TestFlowSpecForwardingKeepsLegacyNextHop (new negative) asserts the same exact zero-hop FlowSpec section beside a legacy unicast section whose own next-hop gate still acts; origination, route-server and wire-contract tests and flow-encode.ci are unchanged and assert zero length. Every distinct cover carries a verified revert record (panic reverts: reachability only, but question 2 is answered by the exact-bytes assertions). Annotation slightly overstates the gap: since f70588873f a 0x0800 voided by an rt-redirect beside it, or stripped at egress, also leaves with length 0; that errs toward disclosure. No test covers the deviation itself, as expected. Scope proven, whole requirement unmet; zero whole-requirement credit.

RFC8955-4.2-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16 after the codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/flowspec; units changed only by package qualification. RFC 8955 Section 4.2: "If present, it MUST precede any component of higher numeric type value." Positive re-parses an out-of-order build and pins the exact emitted order 1,3,5,12 (core writeComponentsSorted); negative feeds 5-then-3 and requires ErrFlowSpecTypeOrder from core parseComponents, with the same components ascending accepted, so the refusal is isolated to order.

RFC8955-4.2-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 by an independent auditor (authored none of 445b2e05f1 or 0474ee945c) after CheckMatchable (internal/core/bgp/nlri/flowspec/unmatchable.go) was rewritten. RFC 8955 Section 4.2: "A specific packet is considered to match the Flow Specification when it matches the intersection (AND) of all the components present in the Flow Specification." and "However, some combinations cannot match any packets (e.g., "ICMP Type AND Port" will never match any packets) and thus SHOULD NOT be propagated by BGP." The earlier finding is closed: every condition the component sections state as "never matches when" is now refused where it can be decided from the NLRI. Transport components needing disjoint protocols (port {6,17}, ICMP {1} or ICMPv6 {58} per RFC 8956 Sections 3.4/3.5, TCP flags {6}, Sections 4.2.2.4, 4.2.2.7-4.2.2.9); a protocol (IPv6 upper-layer) component whose operator expression, evaluated over 0..255 with the Section 4.2.1.1 AND-over-OR precedence, admits none of the needed protocols; and a fragment component admitting neither an unfragmented packet nor a first fragment (states 0 and FF, with DF on IPv4 only, matching the Section 4.2.2.12 and RFC 8956 Section 3.6 bit definitions) beside a transport component. The "unable to locate the transport header" clause is implementation-dependent by the RFC's own words and is not a static contradiction. Tests assert the behaviour exactly: TestCheckMatchable checks 35 cases built, read from the wire, as VPN and VPN from the wire with errors.Is equality, each refusal beside its nearest matchable control (protocol >=6 AND <=17 vs >6 AND <17, icmp OR udp, !=6 with port vs tcp-flags, is-fragment OR first-fragment, DF AND IsF); TestFlowSpecUnmatchableRefused and TestFlowSpecUnmatchableByValueRefused cover the config route parser and the update text encoder; TestFlowSpecUnmatchableReceivedRuleIsNotPropagated, TestFlowSpecUnmatchableReceivedRuleWithdraw and TestFlowSpecUnmatchableByValueReceivedRuleIsNotPropagated pin RouteEligible false, retention, no install event and no candidate on receive (reconcileFlowSpecs via flowSpecDestination) with an eligible control; flowspec-unmatchable-refused.ci refuses through ze config validate. Polarity pairs are genuine and isolate the rule. The 12 discrimination records verify under ./le rfc check (mutants on CheckMatchable lines 67 and 89 both directions; panic reverts on flowSpecDestination and for the .ci prove reach only, their exact assertions answer question 2 by reading); the fragment branch carries no recorded mutant, but TestCheckMatchable's fragment negatives would redden by reading. The finding remains question 4, narrowed to one class: a contradiction in the VALUES of the three port components. Section 4.2.2.4: "This component matches if either the destination port OR the source port of an IP packet matches the value." A rule carrying port =80, destination-port =443 and source-port =443 needs a packet whose destination and source are both 443 and one of which is 80, so it matches no packet; CheckMatchable never reads a port operator list (matches is asked only for the protocol and fragment components), and a probe on the built and wire-parsed FlowSpec returned nil for it while ICMP+port was refused. In general the rule is unmatchable when the port component admits no value the destination-port admits and none the source-port admits. No tagged test would fail if this route is originated or propagated, and the row carries no {partial} scope, so the tags claim the whole SHOULD NOT. To reach enforced, either CheckMatchable compares the port list with the destination-port and source-port lists (over 0..65535) with a negative and a matchable control, or the row is narrowed to {partial} with this as its gap. Not counted as a miss of this row: a single component whose own operator list admits no value (e.g. fragment FF AND IsF alone, an IPv6 upper-layer value that is an extension header, DSCP above 63), because Section 4.2 speaks of combinations of components. Implemented-and-tested: protocol and fragment contradictions on origination and receive, IPv4, IPv6 and VPN. Unimplemented: the port-value contradiction above. The ExaBGP bridge and migration paths pass nil values (types only) and carry no tag here.

RFC8955-4.2.1.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21: the unit changed only in its doc comment, which now names parseNumericTermsText, the parser the config path reaches through parseFlowNumericMatches since 6fac9359ff. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.1.1: "In the first operator octet of a sequence, it MUST be encoded as unset." Single-polarity positive: config range '>8080&<8088' encodes two ops and the test asserts the first carries AND clear (0x40) and the second set, so an encoder setting AND on the first operator goes red. parseNumericTermsText refuses a token starting with & when no term precedes it, so no input sets the first AND bit.

RFC8955-4.2.1.1-2.note: Independent rejudge 2026-10-17, upgraded from weak because a new tagged unit closes the encode clause. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.1.1: "In the first operator octet of a sequence, it MUST be encoded as unset and MUST be treated as always unset on decoding." Decode: TestRFC8955FirstOperatorAndBitTreatedUnsetOnDecode (both tags) requires identical [[=80],[=22]] JSON with the leading AND bit clear and set. Encode: TestRFC8955TextLeadingAndEncodedUnset drives EncodeFlowSpecComponents, the live text encoder behind the registered InProcessNLRIEncoder (register.go) and OnEncodeNLRI; parseBitmaskValue sets FlowMatch.And from the '&' prefix and NewFlowTCPFlagsMatchComponent stores it unmodified, so "&syn" reaches core numericComponent.writeToAFI as a first match with And set, and only the `i > 0 && m.And` guard keeps 0x40 off. The exact 03 09 80 02 assertion goes red (0xc0) if the guard is reduced to `m.And`; the contrast case (syn &ack -> 00 02 c0 10) shows the encoder does set AND at i>0, so the assertion is about position. writeToAFI is shared by FlowSpec.WriteTo (types.go) for config-built rules too. The recorded break (whole writeToAFI panics) proves reach only; the guard-specific red is established by reading.

RFC8955-4.2.1.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved verbatim to core compare_rfc8955_test.go, with only the family identifier renamed. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.1.1: "0: MUST be set to 0 on NLRI encoding and MUST be ignored during decoding". Wire op 0xf9 carries the reserved bit 0x08 and a leading AND. The positive requires the exact decoded []FlowMatch{{Op: FlowOpEqual, Value: 1<<56|7}}, so the reserved bit is ignored by core parseNumericComponent's 0x07 mask. The negative requires re-encoding to the exact op 0xb1, so reserved and leading AND are cleared by writeToAFI, and a missing end-of-list bit is refused.

RFC8955-4.2.1.2-1.note: Re-judged again 2026-10-16 after a comment-only edit. The new VALIDATES claim that parseNumericComponent masks 0x0C is TRUE: core types_numeric.go computes compOp = op & 0x03 for FlowTCPFlags and FlowFragment. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.1.2: "0 (all 0 bits): MUST be set to 0 on NLRI encoding and MUST be ignored during" decoding. Encode: assert.Zero(op&0x0C) over every emitted TCP-flags operator (MATCH, NOT, AND+END) goes red if the length, AND, END, NOT or MATCH bits move into 0x0C. The inputs carry no reserved bits, so deleting the 0x03 mask in core writeToAFI alone stays green. That mask is defence in depth: no reachable producer sets 0x0C, because parseBitmaskValue (text) and parseFlowTCPFlagMatches (config) build only NOT/MATCH, and parseNumericComponent masks received ops to 0x03. Decode: op 0x8D must render exactly like 0x81 (=syn) through the plugin JSON path, with the clean render pinned first. The decode proof is at the rendered match, not at the firewall lowering.

RFC8955-4.2.2.10-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: same units and same change as RFC8955-4.2.2.5-1. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.10: "Type 10 component values SHOULD be encoded as 1- or 2-octet quantities (numeric_op len=00 or len=01)." Packet-length emission requires exact one- and two-octet operands at 0/255/256/65535 across the typed, generic, config and text producers, plus recipient forwarding. Single-polarity as annotated, and the shortest width is local policy. Second re-judgement 2026-10-16: TestFlowSpecPreferredNumericEmission's typed packet-length producer is now the test helper packetLengthComponent (plugin types_test.go), which builds FlowMatch{Op: FlowOpEqual, Value: v} through NewFlowNumericComponent(FlowPacketLength, ...). That is byte-for-byte the matches that the deleted NewFlowPacketLengthComponent built at HEAD (plugin types_numeric.go:457-463). The deleted constructor had no non-test caller at HEAD, so no production producer lost coverage. The typed and generic cases now drive the same constructor, and the registered config, text and forwarding producers carry the distinct evidence.

RFC8955-4.2.2.11-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit changed only in a comment path. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.11: "Type 11 component values MUST be encoded as single octet (numeric_op len=00)." Single-polarity positive: DSCP 46, 0 and 63 through the config producer each encode as exactly one octet. Core parseNumericComponent also refuses a DSCP valueLen other than 1 on receipt.

RFC8955-4.2.2.12-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21: the unit changed only in its doc comment, which now names parseFlowFragmentMatches (config reads parseBitmaskValue since 6fac9359ff). RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.12: "The Type 12 component bitmask MUST be encoded as single octet bitmask (bitmask_op len=00)." Single-polarity positive: all four fragment flags through the config producer encode as exactly one-octet values. parseBitmaskValue holds every operand in a uint8 (names are low-nibble flags, a number is bounded to 255 by parseUint8), and core writeToAFI masks fragment values before choosing a width, so no wider bitmask is reachable.

RFC8955-4.2.2.12-2.note: Independent rejudge 2026-10-17, upgraded from weak because a new tagged unit drives the IPv4 mask. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.12, of the four high bits of the fragment bitmask: "0: MUST be set to 0 on NLRI encoding and MUST be ignored during decoding". Decode: TestRFC8955FragmentReservedBitsIgnoredOnDecode requires 0xF2 to render exactly as 0x02. Encode: TestRFC8955TextFragmentIPv4ReservedBitsCleared feeds "fragment 242" and "fragment 255" through EncodeFlowSpecComponents (the live text encoder); parseBitmaskValue/parseUint8 accept 0..255 and NewFlowFragmentMatchComponent stores the value unmodified, so the reserved nibble reaches core writeToAFI, where `m.Value &= fragmentMask(AFIIPv4)` (0x0f) is the only clearing step. The exact octets 0x02 and 0x0f go red (0xf2, 0xff) if that step is removed, and 0x0f also distinguishes the IPv4 mask from the IPv6 0x0e (DF kept). TestFlowSpecFragmentReservedHighNibbleZero stays tagged but alone cannot fail (named constants only); the row no longer depends on it. The recorded break (fragmentMask panics) proves reach; the mask-specific red is established by reading.

RFC8955-4.2.2.9-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit changed only in a comment path (core types_numeric.go). RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.9: "Type 9 component bitmasks MUST be encoded as 1- or 2-octet bitmask (bitmask_op len=00 or len=01)." Single-polarity positive, as annotated: every emitted tcp-flags bitmask from the config producer (buildFlowSpecComponents with AND, NOT and OR terms) must be non-empty and at most 2 octets.

RFC8955-5.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved verbatim to core compare_rfc8955_test.go, with only the family identifier renamed. RFC 8955 Section 5.1: "This ordering function is such that it does not depend on the arrival order of the Flow Specification via BGP and thus is consistent in the network." Compare is required to be antisymmetric and reflexive (a<b, b>a, a==a) over type, prefix, operator-byte and width pairs. Core Compare reads only component content (no peer, time or action). The arrival-order sort itself is exercised by RFC5575-5.1-1's TestRFC5575PrecedenceIndependentOfArrival, which this row does not tag.

RFC8955-5.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the compare unit moved verbatim to core and the flowspec-firewall kernel unit is unchanged. RFC 8955 Section 5.1: "The relative order of two Flow Specifications is determined by comparing their respective components." TestFlowSpecPrecedenceFromWire pins, with forward and reverse signs and self equality, each of these: a lower type first, a present-versus-absent next component, a more-specific overlapping prefix first, a lower disjoint prefix first, equal-width memcmp, and received-width bytes over numeric value. TestSelectedFlowSpecKernelPacketSemantics adds Linux packet evidence that the more-specific terminal rule wins over a covering discard in either install order. That unit needs integration+linux privileges, and a skipped run is not runtime proof. The clause "If the common prefix is equal, the longest string is considered to have higher precedence" has no pair.
